caption: Be honest, is your castor oil sitting in the cupboard right now? 🙋‍♀️ That was me. author: irockluxurybeauty
caption: 🌿 CASTOR OIL: One Oil… SO Many Uses! 🌿 If you’re going to use castor oil, the TYPE matters! ✨ What to look for: ✔️ 100% pure castor oil ✔️ Cold-pressed ✔️ Hexane-free ✔️ Organic when possible ✔️ Packaged in a dark glass bottle to protect the oil from light 💚 WAYS I LOVE USING CASTOR OIL: ✨ Hair & Scalp — Helps moisturize dry hair and scalp and can reduce breakage by keeping hair conditioned. ✨ Eyebrows — A tiny amount can condition dry, brittle eyebrow hairs and make them look fuller and healthier. ✨ Skin Moisturizer — Rich in fatty acids, especially ricinoleic acid, making it great for sealing moisture into dry areas. ✨ Cuticles, Hands & Feet — Amazing for rough heels, dry hands and cracked-looking cuticles. ✨ Massage Oil — Its thick consistency makes it useful for massaging dry or tight-feeling areas. ✨ Castor Oil Packs — Some people apply castor oil to cloth and place it over the abdomen as part of a traditional wellness routine. Evidence for claims such as “detoxing the liver” or shrinking lumps is limited, so I wouldn’t make those promises. ✨ Constipation — Castor oil is also an FDA-recognized stimulant laxative when taken orally, but drinking castor oil is completely different from applying it to your skin. It can cause strong cramping and diarrhea, so follow product directions and check with your healthcare provider when appropriate. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: “Black castor oil” and regular cold-pressed castor oil aren’t exactly the same. For a simple, minimally processed option for skin or castor-oil packs, I’d choose 100% pure, cold-pressed, hexane-free castor oil. 💡 Always patch test first. And remember—natural doesn’t automatically mean risk-free. Who else keeps castor oil in their wellness cabinet? 🌿👇🏽 #CastorOil #holistic  #wellness       #creatorsearchinsights
